manager_rule: Track a persistent mapping 'priority_contamination_streak': the key is the frozenset of net names removed as over-targeted in a Rule 23 (stale_targeting_same_round_corrected) log entry; the value is the count of consecutive Rule 23 firings in which that exact frozenset appeared as the removed over-targeted nets. Increment the count when the current Rule 23 firing's removed-nets frozenset matches the immediately prior Rule 23 firing's removed-nets frozenset; reset a frozenset's count to 1 when it appears after having been absent for at least one intervening round. When priority_contamination_streak reaches 3 for any frozenset S, the manager MUST: (1) add every net in S to a session-scoped exclusion list 'compiler_excluded_nets'; (2) instruct the stub compiler to unconditionally omit every net in compiler_excluded_nets from its candidate set for all remaining rounds of the session, regardless of accumulated priority score or decay state; (3) log 'priority_contamination_exclusion' with fields: (a) round number, (b) the excluded frozenset S, (c) streak length = 3, (d) the round numbers in which that frozenset appeared as the stale over-targeted set. This exclusion is permanent for the session and does not require human clearance, because all nets in S are demonstrably non-critical (each firing of Rule 23 already classified them as non-critical CAN/I2C-class), their repeated identical appearance after per-round correction demonstrates a structural priority-model bias beyond incremental repair, and no net in S is a Kelvin, diffpair, or other hard-gated net, so exclusion cannot block a gate. If after applying compiler_excluded_nets the compiler's residual candidate set is empty for any round, the manager MUST immediately escalate with log 'compiler_candidate_set_exhausted_post_exclusion', reporting the full compiler_excluded_nets list and the compiler's current priority weight table, and halt FR dispatch pending human inspection.
